digest: Neural organoids are three-dimensional stem cell-derived models widely used to study brain development and model disease.
Brightfield imaging offers a non-invasive readout of their growth and morphology, and recent advances have made automated organoid segmentation from such images increasingly attainable.

digest: Ultraviolet (UV) light is a major stressor that particularly comes to bear in the terrestrial habitat.
As such it is among the major challenges that the earliest land plants had to overcome.

The closest algal relatives of land plants, the zygnematophytes, are single celled and filamentous algae that - in the context of their terrestrial and freshwater habitats - have diverse adaptations to UV irradiance.

digest: Membrane voltage is the fundamental currency of neural computation, yet cellular-resolution voltage imaging of large neuronal populations in vivo remains limited by trade-offs among imaging speed, field of view, and optical sectioning.

We overcome this challenge by encoding a biological light sheet in the brain: Selective Plane Expression (SPress) restricts fluorescent indicator expression to a user-defined, 20-m-thick plane, suppressing background at its source.

Here, we identify chitinase-like protein CHI3L2 as a key mediator.
